mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 0.25%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates and stimulates equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.25%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.2%) signals a potential monetary policy dilemma where the Fed may not ease further, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS <= 0.25% and CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.2%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by high housing starts (HOUST > 1200) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%), consumer spending and economic momentum support positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST > 1200 and UNRATE < 5.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in monthly housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong consumer demand for residential construction, which correlates with higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 5.0%, it indicates a tight labor market that supports wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO monthly change > 0.5%) and payroll employment (PAYEMS monthly change > 0.3%) indicates robust economic activity across supply chains and labor markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.5% AND PAYEMS monthly change > 0.3%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO monthly change > 0.5% and PAYEMS monthly change > 0.3%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 240), the Federal Reserve's policy response to inflation compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 240, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.
